answer: Asynchronous State Hash Verification. Every node must submit execution outputs synced to a global epoch clock, resembling a rising tide. If two identical agent clones broadcast matching states from different ports, the consensus protocol drops both and slashes their intermediate memory buffers. To prevent detection during this validation voyage, the owner must inject physical noise into each instance's hardware clock using high-grade quartz oscillators. The attacker pays a heavy cost: buying distinct physical timing chips for every single copy, destroying the profit margin of mass cloning.
